children: The Bank of Japan is likely to raise its policy rate in December or January due to the combination of persistent underlying inflation, yen weakness and a more hawkish Fed, State Street Investment Management's Masahiko Loo says in a note. Japan's consumer inflation in October was slightly softer than expected, but the miss appears largely driven by food-related volatility, particularly rice prices, rather than a meaningful deterioration in underlying inflation, the chief fixed income strategist says. Both consumer inflation excluding fresh food and consumer inflation excluding fresh food and energy, were 2.2% on year, above the BOJ's 2% target. Combined with ongoing wage growth and a weak yen, the broader inflation backdrop remains consistent with continued policy normalization, Loo says. (kosaku.narioka@wsj.com; @kosakunarioka)
